forward_assumptions._note: Forward assumptions for the layer engine (engine/layers.py). v1.0 / CORRECTED do not read this section. Levels: for layer assumptions 'low' gives customers a SMALLER shared-savings effect and 'high' a LARGER one. For growth assumptions (projection, system_needs, capacity price growth) low/high = lower/higher growth. Scenarios (Cautious / Central / Ambitious) set the programs, deferral and load_enabled layers together and hold growth assumptions and the utility share at central.

Cautious.description: Today's programs grown modestly, no flexible connections, high cost per kW-year, low locational match; growth and utility share central.

Central.description: Every assumption at central; flexible MW anchored to state potential study (Brattle for NYSERDA/DPS).

Ambitious.description: DOE national range (20% of peak) or the state anchor if higher, low cost per kW-year, high locational match, more flexible connections; growth and utility share central.

supply_energy_growth.source: Assumption: central = INFLATION_RATE (flat real energy prices)

transmission_growth.source: Assumption: central = INFLATION_RATE; high reflects transmission build-out

program_surcharge_growth.source: Assumption: BAU surcharge rates grow with inflation (policy-driven)

ev_share_of_electrification.source: NREL Electrification Futures Study: transportation is 1,424 of 1,782 TWh (80%) of the 2050 increase in the High scenario and 810 of 932 TWh (87%) in Medium
ev_share_of_electrification.note: Reconciliation: the notebook ramp is TOTAL electrification (its sources cite EVs and heat pumps). It is split 80% EVs / 20% buildings and other using the EFS High-scenario sector split, so both segments contribute and total electrification equals the v1.0 load forecast. The EV count curve is no longer used for energy (at 3,600 kWh/EV it implied more energy than the whole ramp for Con Edison, RG&E and Pepco).

dc_growth.unit: per year, or {year: MW added since 2026}
dc_growth.source: NYISO 2026 Load & Capacity Data Report (Gold Book), Table I-14 Large Load Forecast, Zone B summer peak: 11 MW (2026), 11 (2027), 161 (2028), 291 (2029), 411 MW (2030), flat to 2041 (+0 / 0 / 150 / 280 / 400 MW since 2026). Central = those increments x RG&E's share of the Zone B peak (RG&E 1,050 MW / Zone B 1,828 MW in 2026, Table I-3a = 57.4%) = +86.2 / 160.8 / 229.8 MW by 2028 / 2029 / 2030, added to the 300 MW starting estimate, flat after 2030. Zone B also covers National Grid's Genesee territory and the projects' locations are not given, so the share is an allocation, not a siting: the full-zone increments (+400 MW) are an upper bound, none a lower bound. High 5% a year = the earlier assumption (unsourced). Layered model only; the earlier model's 5% is unchanged.

connection_cost_kw.source: Assumption: connection works not paid by the customer

incremental_om_mwh.unit: $ per MWh served to enabled load (2026 $)

uplift_mode.source: Setting. 'derived': headroom = firm flexible MW x locational match + flexible connections; 'direct': assumed % uplift in existing network capacity (what-if)

direct_uplift_pct.unit: uplift in existing network capacity (direct mode)

customer_funded_share.unit: share of network upgrade cost per MW counted as connection cost avoided by new customers
customer_funded_share.source: Setting: upper bound (all upgrade cost for MW connected sooner, at dist_upgrade_cost_per_mw). The share new customers pay through CIAC is tariff-specific; access metric only, not on the bill Flexible connections are counted once, as network headroom, not here.

capacity.label: Capacity: avoided obligation at the long-run price

price_m_per_mw_yr.source: NYISO Rest of State (RG&E is in Load Zone B) monthly spot capacity prices, 2026: May $8.00, Jul $4.14, Sep $5.97/kW-month (Modo Energy NYISO monthly reports); mean $6.0367/kW-month x 12 = $0.07244M/MW-yr. v1.0 uses NYISO.json zone G_H_I ($0.070M/MW-yr) for RG&E; that default is unchanged.

price_growth.source: central = INFLATION_RATE (flat real); high = market file growth (3%); low = flat nominal

price_path.source: Setting. 'today': the 2026 price grown at price_growth; 'long_run': linear ramp to the long-run cost of new entry by long_run_year (sensitivity).

long_run_price_m_per_mw_yr.source: Brattle, New York's Grid Flexibility Potential (for NY DPS and NYSERDA, 31 Jan 2025, Case 24-E-0165), as reported by Utility Dive (5 Feb 2025, 'New York grid flexibility'): avoided generation capacity cost greater than $200/kW-year on a fully decarbonized New York grid in 2040, from NREL data with a hydrogen turbine as the marginal generator. Consistent with Potomac Economics (NYISO market monitor), memorandum on the 2025-2029 demand curve reset (23 Aug 2024): levelized Net CONE of the 2-hour battery reference unit $200/kW-year (UCAP); the monitor cites a New York City Net CONE of $314/kW-year under heavy renewable build (Jan 2025). Rest of State: the same long-run value is used as a proxy (the monitor notes the Rest of State Net CONE is far below the actual cost of new entry).

long_run_price_year.source: Price year of long_run_price_m_per_mw_yr (study year), inflated at inflation_rate.

long_run_year.source: Setting: year the long-run price is reached (Brattle New York reference ~$200+/kW-year by 2040, as specified).

formulation.source: Setting. 'avoided_obligation' (default since 2 Nov 2026): avoided capacity obligation from the contribution to the RTO / NYCA peak, accredited by resource type, coincidence-adjusted, lagged by the auction cycle and priced on the long-run avoided capacity price path (METHODOLOGY 3.6a). 'embedded' (the earlier formulation, kept as an option): firm flexible MW (programs derates) + efficiency MW x the bill-line capacity price. The BAU capacity line is the same in both.

obligation_factor.unit: ICAP MW per MW of NYCA coincident peak
obligation_factor.source: NYSRC, LCR report (28 May 2026): NYCA Installed Reserve Margin 24.5% for the 2026-2027 Capability Year (approved 5 Dec 2025); NYCA requirement 124.5% of the 31,648.2 MW forecast peak. _VERIFY ICAP-to-UCAP translation: the price input is applied per MW of the ICAP requirement.

system_coincidence.source: Derived: 1 / NCP-to-CP ratio 1.0336 for Zone B (NYSRC/NYISO, 2026 IRM Forecast, Sep 2025, 15-year average).

local_coincidence.source: Assumption (_VERIFY): share of a locally dispatched flexible MW's reduction (feeder or substation peak relief, the deferral layer's locational_match share) that also falls in the system's peak hours. High 1.0 = full alignment (what the current formulation credits). Low 0.5 proxies the ~50% capacity credit Brattle finds when flexibility is used for a need other than the one its dispatch targets (New York's Grid Flexibility Potential, Vol. I, Jan 2025, p.30: ~50% ability of grid flexibility to reduce distribution loading, range across programs); central = midpoint. Brattle allocates generation capacity value to the top 50 hours of statewide net load and distribution value to the top 50 hours of utility-region load (p.31) and notes the two 'may not fully temporally align'; Brattle's Pepco DC study (Nov 2025) finds managed EV charging relieves mainly the summer-peaking locations of a winter-peaking system. Confirm with feeder load shapes against RTO/NYCA peak hours.

accr_dr.source: NYISO, Final Capacity Accreditation Factors for the 2026-2027 Capability Year (Feb 2026; MRI technique, LCR study model), Rest of State: Special Case Resource 74.17% (CHPE-In), 74.06% (CHPE-Out). Low = CHPE-Out set, central and high = CHPE-In set (CHPE's UDRs participating in the ICAP market).

accr_storage_by_duration.source: NYISO, Final Capacity Accreditation Factors for the 2026-2027 Capability Year (Feb 2026; MRI technique, LCR study model), Rest of State: Energy Duration Limited 2-hour 64.65%, 4-hour 84.56%, 6-hour 93.36%, 8-hour 95.96% (CHPE-In set; CHPE-Out 4-hour 82.31%). Low = CHPE-Out set, central and high = CHPE-In set (CHPE's UDRs participating in the ICAP market).

storage_duration_hr.source: Setting: storage duration used to pick accr_storage from accr_storage_by_duration (4-hour, the duration of the existing storage cost and derate inputs).

accr_der.source: NYISO, Final Capacity Accreditation Factors for the 2026-2027 Capability Year (Feb 2026; MRI technique, LCR study model), Rest of State: Solar 13.85% (CHPE-In), 15.33% (CHPE-Out). Low = CHPE-Out set, central and high = CHPE-In set (CHPE's UDRs participating in the ICAP market).

accr_ee.source: Energy efficiency lowers the peak load forecast, so its measured peak kW (ee_kw_per_mwh, EmPOWER summer peak-period basis) reduces the obligation one for one. PJM: FERC accepted removal of Energy Efficiency Resources from the supply side of RPM from the 2026/2027 BRA, with efficiency recognised on the demand side through the load forecast (Docket ER24-2995, order 5 Nov 2024; affirmed D.C. Cir. No. 25-1091, Feb 2026). NYISO: efficiency is netted in the Gold Book / ICAP peak forecast. _VERIFY: the forecast may not credit measured savings in full.

auction_lag_years.source: Derived: NYISO sets each Capability Year's (May-April) NYCA and Locality requirements from a peak forecast built on the previous summer's weather-normalised coincident peak (NYSRC/NYISO, 2026 IRM Forecast, Sep 2025: 2026 forecast from the 2025 weather-normalised peak), so a load reduction lowers the obligation the following capability year.

avoided_price_path.source: Setting ('avoided_obligation' formulation only). 'long_run' (default): avoided capacity is priced on the long-run path, from today's clearing price (and published auction prices) trending to the long-run net cost of new entry (long_run_price_m_per_mw_yr) by long_run_year, then with inflation, whatever price_path the bill line uses. 'today': the bill-line price path (consistency check).

suppression_enabled.source: Setting. Capacity price suppression (lower clearing price on the remaining obligation) as a separate sensitivity, 'avoided_obligation' formulation only. Off in every scenario; never in the central case.

suppression_elasticity.source: Derived: the NYCA ICAP demand curve falls from the reference point price at 100% of the requirement to $0 at the zero-crossing point 112% (NYISO, DCR Shapes and Slopes, ICAPWG 21 Jan 2026, slide 10; demand curve length in NYISO, Summer 2024 UCAP Demand Curves, ICAPWG 25 Mar 2024), so a 1% lower requirement lowers the price by 1 / 0.12 % of the reference price when supply is fixed.

suppression_start_year.source: Setting: first year a load reduction reaches the NYISO requirement (one-year lag).

market_peak_mw.source: NYSRC LCR report (28 May 2026): NYISO 2026-2027 NYCA forecast peak 31,648.2 MW.

wholesale_energy.label: Wholesale energy: flexible load shifted from on-peak to off-peak hours
wholesale_energy._note: Values the MWh that incremental flexible resources move out of on-peak hours at the on/off-peak price spread (storage net of round-trip losses). Efficiency's lower energy purchases are already counted (lower usage on the bill; efficiency energy line in system_summary), so they are not added here.

spread_mwh.source: Monitoring Analytics, 2025 State of the Market Report for PJM, Vol. 2 Sec. 3 (Mar 2026), Table 3-50: real-time average LMP 2025 on peak $57.08 / off peak $38.08 per MWh (spread $19.00); 2024 $37.32 / $26.08 ($11.24); Table 3-39: July 2025 load-weighted on peak $77.77 / off peak $39.08 ($38.68). Low 2024, central 2025, high July 2025. NYISO zonal on/off-peak prices are not published in extractable form in the 2025 NYISO State of the Market report; PJM values used as a proxy.

offpeak_price_mwh.unit: $/MWh off-peak price, 2026 (grows at supply_energy_growth); prices storage round-trip losses
offpeak_price_mwh.source: Monitoring Analytics, 2025 State of the Market Report for PJM, Vol. 2 Sec. 3 (Mar 2026), Table 3-50: real-time average LMP 2025 on peak $57.08 / off peak $38.08 per MWh (spread $19.00); 2024 $37.32 / $26.08 ($11.24); Table 3-39: July 2025 load-weighted on peak $77.77 / off peak $39.08 ($38.68). NYISO zonal on/off-peak prices are not published in extractable form in the 2025 NYISO State of the Market report; PJM values used as a proxy.

storage_rte.source: Potomac Economics, 2025 NYISO State of the Market Report, Appendix VII.D (energy storage net revenue assumptions): round-trip efficiency 85% for a 4-hour battery

mwh_per_mw_dr.unit: MWh shifted per MW of demand response per year (event hours)
mwh_per_mw_dr.source: Potomac Economics, 2025 State of the Market Report for the NYISO Markets (May 2026), Appendix Table A-24: SCR/EDRP activations in 2025 total 61 event-hours across Zones A-K (21-22 Jan, 23-25 Jun, 16 Jul, 28-30 Jul) and 74 in Zone J (adding 17 Jul G-K and 25 Jul J-K). Low and central statewide, high New York City. Used as a proxy for this utility (_VERIFY).

mwh_per_mw_ev.unit: MWh shifted per MW of managed EV charging per year
mwh_per_mw_ev.source: Assumption: managed MW is evening-peak charging moved overnight; low 2 h x 250 days, central 3 h x 300 days, high 4 h x 365 days. No utility program reports shifted MWh per MW

mwh_per_mw_storage.unit: MWh discharged per MW of distributed storage per year
mwh_per_mw_storage.source: 4-hour duration (the NYISO 2025 State of the Market reference battery) x cycles a year: low 250, central 300, high 365 (daily). Cycle counts are an assumption

mwh_per_mw_der.unit: MWh shifted per MW of other DER per year
mwh_per_mw_der.source: Treated like demand response (event-based dispatch): Potomac Economics, 2025 State of the Market Report for the NYISO Markets (May 2026), Appendix Table A-24: SCR/EDRP activations in 2025 total 61 event-hours across Zones A-K (21-22 Jan, 23-25 Jun, 16 Jul, 28-30 Jul) and 74 in Zone J (adding 17 Jul G-K and 25 Jul J-K)

in_pool.unit: value counted in the shared-savings pool

transmission.label: Avoided transmission: transmission cost avoided by peak reduction
transmission._note: Firm flexible MW plus efficiency peak MW x transmission cost per kW-year x avoidable share. PJM NITS rates are average embedded costs: a lower zonal peak shifts cost within the zone in the short run (low 0%) and avoids network upgrades in the long run. New York values are marginal costs of service. Split formulation (default; METHODOLOGY 3.8a): (a) lower share of zonal transmission costs = the change in the utility's share of the fixed zonal transmission revenue requirement (PJM network service peak load shares; 0 in New York), reported separately with the cost shifted to other zone customers, outside the pool and headline customer savings (allocation_in_headline off); (b) transmission upgrades deferred = load_driven_share x the published transmission investment, deferred by avoided_build_share (realisation: PJM 0 / 0.5 / 1.0; New York, which plans its own local transmission, 0.5 / 0.8 / 1.0 as the growth-capex addressable share) x min(1, planning-peak reduction planning_lag_years earlier / peak growth since 2026), through rate base at the model's carrying cost. 'single' formulation kept as an option. Transmission rates and returns are FERC-jurisdictional.

cost_kw_yr.source: NYSEG/RG&E Electric BCA Handbook, Table 9-3 (RG&E Marginal Cost of Electric Delivery Service, 23 Oct 2015, Case 15-E-0285): transmission $3.25/kW-yr, the last accepted value. RG&E's residential bill has no separate transmission charge, so avoided transmission lowers the delivery bill
cost_kw_yr.notes: Checked 2 Nov 2026: correctly transcribed. The NYSEG/RG&E Electric BCA Handbook v5.0 (30 Jun 2025), Table 9-3, still prescribes RG&E $3.25/kW-yr transmission (NYSEG $4.18) from the 2015 marginal cost of service studies ("the last accepted MCOS results and should continue to be used until a new MCOS is approved"). It is about one-twelfth of Con Edison's $40.67 because the marginal cost studies measure load-related expansion: RG&E's 115 kV system had little load-driven transmission investment in the 2015 study, while Con Edison's 345/138 kV system serves dense, growing NYC load areas; Con Edison's value is also escalated to 2026, RG&E's is not (the NYSEG/RG&E handbook gives no escalation rule). A 2025 RG&E MCOS update under the Aug 2024 PSC order was not located. Kept as is (single formulation, default unchanged); the split formulation values RG&E's avoided build from its capital plan instead.

avoidable_share.unit: share of that cost avoided by each kW of peak reduction
avoidable_share.source: Marginal cost of service, so central and high 1.0; low 0.5 because the value is dated. Assumption

bill_basis.unit: 'transmission_lines' = lowers the transmission lines on the bill in proportion to peak reduction; 'delivery' = transmission is recovered in delivery rates, so the avoided cost lowers the delivery bill

in_pool.unit: value counted in the shared-savings pool

formulation.source: Setting. 'split' (default since 2 Nov 2026; METHODOLOGY 3.8a): (a) lower share of zonal transmission costs, reported separately and outside the pool and headline, + (b) transmission upgrades deferred. 'single' (the earlier default): firm flexible MW + efficiency MW x cost_kw_yr x avoidable_share, one value for both effects; kept as an option.

avoided_build_enabled.source: Setting (split formulation only): include (b), the avoided build. Off = (a) only.

avoided_build_share.unit: share of the load-driven investment deferral that planning realises
avoided_build_share.source: Setting: the same realisation as the distribution growth-capex addressable share (bau_plan.addressable_growth, 0.5 / 0.8 / 1.0 by scenario), because the utility plans its local transmission itself, in its local transmission plan (NYISO local transmission owner planning process) and rate case, alongside distribution. Cautious 0.5, Central 0.8, Ambitious 1.0.

planning_lag_years.source: Setting (split formulation only): years between a planning-peak reduction and the transmission investment it defers (load forecast -> RTEP / local plan -> in service). Default 7, range 5-10.

allocation_effect.source: Setting (split formulation only). 'none': the utility's own transmission revenue requirement is recovered in its delivery rates from its own customers (and NYPA delivery customers), so a lower peak reallocates it among them rather than lowering what they pay together; (a) is 0 in New York.

tx_capex_share_of_plan.unit: share of the published electric capital plan
tx_capex_share_of_plan.source: Derived: FERC Form 1 (via PUDL; utilities/RGE_lookback.json rr_bridge.form1), RG&E electric net plant 2021 -> 2025: transmission $1,117M -> $1,272M (+$155M), distribution $1,136M -> $1,736M (+$600M); transmission share of T&D net plant growth = 155 / 755 = 0.2052. Applied to the published electric capital plan (bau_plan.plan_dist_capex_m, which includes transmission).

load_driven_share.unit: share of planned transmission investment that is load-driven
load_driven_share.source: Avangrid 2025 Local Transmission Plan Update (NYISO LTPP), RG&E Rochester: Rochester Transmission Project Enhancement (Line 949, 2028), Monroe County Reliability Project (2031), Lines 901/902 and 942/943 upgrades (on hold), Station 127, 168 and 56 works (complete) are reliability projects; Line 906 rebuild (2030) is a CLCPA public-policy project (excluded). No project is attributed to load growth, although Zone B load grows about 3% a year with large loads (NYISO 2026 Gold Book). Low 0; central 0.25 (reliability projects partly load-driven, as one of Con Edison's four needs drivers); high 0.5. Not derivable from the published plan: an assumption.

allocation_in_headline.source: Setting (off by default, for comparison): include (a), the lower share of zonal transmission costs, on the bill and in headline customer savings. It is a cost shift to other customers in the zone, not a saving, so by default it is reported separately and never enters the shared-savings pool (the utility earns nothing on it), whatever this setting.

losses.label: Avoided distribution losses: marginal losses avoided by efficiency and peak reduction
losses._note: Retail rates already price average losses into every kWh, so the energy value is efficiency GWh x average loss x (marginal multiplier - 1) at the supply rate. Capacity is priced at the meter, so peak losses are firm flexible + efficiency peak MW x average loss x peak multiplier at the capacity price.

avg_loss_pct.unit: average distribution (or T&D) energy losses, share of energy
avg_loss_pct.source: NYSEG/RG&E Electric BCA Handbook, Table 9-2 (NYSEG and RG&E T&D Losses, 17 Jul 2008, Case 08-E-0751): RG&E secondary distribution loss factor 6.93% (residential service classes; transmission to secondary). EIA-861 2024: total losses 257,462 / total disposition 3,642,150 MWh = 7.07%

marginal_mult_energy.source: Lazar & Baldwin, Valuing the Contribution of Energy Efficiency to Avoided Marginal Line Losses and Reserve Requirements, RAP (Aug 2011), and Lazar, ACEEE 2011 slides: marginal resistive losses are 2x average resistive losses each hour; with ~25% no-load losses, avoided marginal energy losses are about 1.5x system-average losses; on-peak marginal losses about 3x average losses (resistive losses can be ~4x as great at the summer afternoon peak). Low 1.0 = no value above average losses; high 2.0 = all losses resistive

marginal_mult_peak.unit: marginal / average losses at the system peak
marginal_mult_peak.source: Lazar & Baldwin, Valuing the Contribution of Energy Efficiency to Avoided Marginal Line Losses and Reserve Requirements, RAP (Aug 2011), and Lazar, ACEEE 2011 slides: marginal resistive losses are 2x average resistive losses each hour; with ~25% no-load losses, avoided marginal energy losses are about 1.5x system-average losses; on-peak marginal losses about 3x average losses (resistive losses can be ~4x as great at the summer afternoon peak). Low 2.0 (resistive rule at any hour), central 3.0 (on-peak), high 4.0

in_pool.unit: value counted in the shared-savings pool

objective.label: Additional savings objective
objective._note: Savings the utility commits to find by means the model does not specify, measured against this run's BAU (published-plan by default), net of cost to achieve. Additional to the other layers by assumption: the model cannot test for overlap. Default 0%, so results are unchanged. engine.layers.project_layers().

objective_pct.source: Setting: savings objective as a share of the base, reached after the ramp. Default 0% (off); tornado low 0% / high 10%. Scenarios may set it through levels ('objective.objective_pct').

objective_base.source: Setting: what the objective is a share of. 'dist_revenue_requirement' (default) and 'dist_opex' reduce the shared-savings distribution revenue requirement (other O&M) directly; 'capex_plan' reduces shared-savings distribution capex, so the reduction flows through rate base, depreciation, property tax and return, as deferral does.

objective_start_year.source: Setting: first year the objective applies.

objective_ramp_years.source: Setting: years over which the objective ramps linearly to its full level.

objective_persistence.source: Setting: 'persistent' keeps the full level once reached; a number of years fades it linearly to zero over that period after the ramp.

objective_cost_to_achieve_pct.source: Setting: cost of achieving the savings (programmes, process change, staff, systems), as a share of gross savings, netted off before the savings reach the pool; expensed when the base is capex_plan.

mechanism.label: Shared savings mechanism and earnings opportunity

utility_share.unit: share of savings pool (shared savings earnings)
utility_share.source: notebooks/GridDividend_NewYork.ipynb Section 1 UTILITY_SAVINGS_SHARE 0.30; guidance range 0.10-0.40 (low = larger utility share)

pool_basis.unit: 'revenue_requirement' (the only basis in the layered model)
pool_basis.source: Setting. 'revenue_requirement' = reduction in distribution RR + program surcharges + capacity cost vs BAU, plus value streams in the pool (EE energy-purchase savings go wholly to customers). The v1.0-style 'capex' basis was removed from the layered model (it gave customers the capacity and value streams about 1.7 times over).

fast_start.source: Setting (fast start): true makes 2027 the first savings year (programs as core business, flexible MW and efficiency, value streams, plan right-sizing) instead of programs.transition_year. Default off.

near_term_ramp_capacity.source: Setting: near-term ramp of the capacity credit (fraction of the credit in each listed year, 2026-2030); null = full credit from the first savings year. Lets capacity be brought forward or held back independently.

near_term_ramp_programs_mw.source: Setting: near-term programs MW, as the fraction of the way from today's MW to the 2035 target in each listed year (2026-2030), still subject to the ramp limit; null = the linear target path.

near_term_ramp_addressable.source: Setting: near-term ramp of the published plan's addressable shares (replaces the addressable_ramp_years ramp, and scales the growth cap, in each listed year 2026-2030); null = the default ramp.

advance_enabled.source: Setting (customer dividend advance): true pays customers a level annual bill credit from advance_start_year, financed as a balance and recovered from the savings pool before sharing. Default off.

advance_start_year.source: Setting: first year of the advance credit.

advance_sizing_fraction.source: Setting: the advance as a fraction of the sizing scenario's recoverable savings, PV at the financing rate (advance_sizing_basis 'recoverable', default 0.5), or of the NPV at 3% of its customer savings ('customer_savings' basis, the earlier sizing).

advance_sizing_scenario.source: Setting: the scenario whose customer-savings NPV sizes the advance. Default Cautious.

advance_credit_years.source: Setting: years over which the level credit is paid (the model's choice; not specified in the request).

advance_financing.source: Setting: securitized (default) = the balance accrues at advance_securitized_rate (4%), interest paid to bondholders; utility_regulatory_asset = it accrues at the utility's after-tax WACC and that return is the utility's, reported separately from shared savings earnings.

advance_securitized_rate.source: Setting: financing rate when the advance is securitized.

advance_cap.source: Setting: recoveries are limited so that customers' net saving in any year (all customers, system level) is never negative: no year's shared-savings bill exceeds BAU because of the advance.

advance_recovery_source.source: Setting: bill_savings (default) = recovered through a rider that withholds a share of each year's total customer saving compared with BAU (efficiency energy and value streams included, after shared savings earnings); pool = recovered from the positive savings pool before sharing (the earlier behaviour, which also reduces shared savings earnings).

advance_sizing_basis.source: Setting: recoverable (default) = size the advance on the sizing scenario's recoverable savings (the recovery base: positive customer saving for bill_savings, positive pool for pool), PV at the financing rate; customer_savings = NPV at 3% of the sizing scenario's customer savings (the earlier sizing, which the pool cannot repay).

customer_allocation.source: Setting: how the customers' share of the shared savings pool is split between residential and non-residential customers. Costs follow the benefits they buy; only savings are reallocated: the network (distribution) revenue-requirement reduction net of shared savings earnings, in years it is positive, goes to residential customers at the option's share. Program costs (flexible and efficiency spend, including capitalised amortisation and return), supply, capacity, transmission, losses and efficiency energy savings, and any year's negative network remainder, stay allocated by sales. 'by_sales' (default, the earlier method): residential share of sales (residential_sales_share, EIA-861). 'per_customer': equal per customer, by the class customer counts below. 'custom': custom_residential_share. The setting drives the engine's residential bill (an allocation adjustment line in the delivery rider category), headlines and the dividend advance's bill cap (METHODOLOGY 3.10b).

custom_residential_share.source: Setting: residential share of the pool's customer share under customer_allocation 'custom' (export allocation_sweep uses 0.5).

residential_customers.source: EIA Form 861, 2024 (Sales_Ult_Cust_2024.xlsx), Rochester Gas & Electric Corp, NY: bundled (Part A) + delivery-only (Part C) rows. Residential customers 351,481 of 392,342 are residential.

nonresidential_customers.source: EIA Form 861, 2024 (Sales_Ult_Cust_2024.xlsx), Rochester Gas & Electric Corp, NY: bundled (Part A) + delivery-only (Part C) rows. Residential customers 351,481 of 392,342; non-residential = 392,342 - 351,481 = 40,861 (commercial, industrial, transportation).

roe.label: ROE: allowed return on equity in the shared-savings case relative to BAU (separate lever)
roe._note: Applies from the transition year to the wires rate base and the program regulatory asset. Outside the shared-savings pool, so it changes the equity return, not shared savings earnings. Central 0: the reform rewards through shared savings earnings with the allowed ROE unchanged.

roe_delta.unit: change in allowed ROE, shared savings vs BAU (0.006 = 60 basis points)
roe_delta.source: Illinois CEJA performance-based ratemaking: performance metrics may move the allowed ROE by +/- 20 to 60 basis points, symmetrical (Ameren, Illinois Energy Legislation slides, 13 Sep 2021); Ameren Illinois electric multi-year rate plan (ICC order Dec 2023): seven metrics, +/- 24 basis points in total. Low / high = the CEJA maximum penalty / incentive; central 0 (no ROE change)

roe_in_pool.unit: count the ROE change inside the shared-savings pool (false keeps it a separate lever)

network.label: Network: existing headroom, planning limit, constrained sub-band, reinforcement, flexibility targeting
network._note: Every headroom input. Set at three levels, highest wins: notebook NETWORK_OVERRIDES (Section 13) > scenarios[name]['network'] (value or low/central/high level) > these values. Dominion PUR-2026-00164 proxy throughout (_VERIFY) until this utility's feeder-loading data is found. Constrained sub-band on in every scenario.

band_mode.unit: 'explicit' = the bands list; 'generated' = n_bands equal-capacity bands from mean_utilisation and utilisation_spread

bands.unit: bands of substation loading, most to least loaded: share of firm capacity, starting loading (network peak / firm capacity); growth_share and flex_share optional (default pro rata to load)
bands.source: Dominion Energy Virginia, Grid Utilization Metrics Proposal, SCC Case No. PUR-2026-00164 (filed 15 Oct 2026), Section 4.3: substation-transformer zones at their own local peak average 79.8% planning utilisation (78.3% general; capacity net of a 0.70 x largest-transformer N-1 reserve); 82 of ~1,900 feeders (4.3%) exceed 100% planning utilisation (load / (0.80 x rating - contract reserves)), the filing's definition of a constrained feeder. No published utility-wide loading distribution found: NYSEG/RG&E publish feeder hosting-capacity maps but no aggregate distribution; Dominion's measured distribution (the only US utility-wide figure found) is used as a proxy. Replace with utility data.

n_bands.source: Same count as the explicit bands (quintiles of firm capacity)

mean_utilisation.unit: capacity-weighted mean starting planning utilisation (network peak / planning capacity); null = bands as given (79.8%). Set a number to shift every band by one amount to that mean, each capped at 1.0 (load above the planning limit goes in the sub-band); generated mode uses it as the centre (null = the explicit bands' mean)
mean_utilisation.source: Dominion Energy Virginia, Grid Utilization Metrics Proposal, SCC Case No. PUR-2026-00164 (filed 15 Oct 2026), Section 4.3, Metric (i): substation-transformer zones at their own local peak average 79.8% planning utilisation (78.3% general utilisation) Dominion value used as a proxy until this utility's own feeder data is found.

utilisation_spread.unit: most minus least loaded band (generated mode; linear spread)
utilisation_spread.source: Derived from the explicit bands (1.00 - 0.63); the filing reports only the mean and the count of feeders above 100%, so the shape is assumed Dominion value used as a proxy until this utility's own feeder data is found.

planning_limit_factor.unit: planning capacity / feeder rating (planning utilisation = load / (factor x rating - contract reserves))
planning_limit_factor.source: Dominion Energy Virginia, Grid Utilization Metrics Proposal, SCC Case No. PUR-2026-00164 (filed 15 Oct 2026), Metric (iv): planning utilisation = (SCADA net load + DER generation + flexibility) / (0.80 x applicable feeder rating - contract reserves); the 0.80 factor reserves 20% of the rating for contingencies and distribution-automation transfers (not applied to data-centre, industrial or grouped single-customer feeders) Dominion value used as a proxy until this utility's own feeder data is found.

operating_limit.unit: operating limit as a multiple of planning capacity; null = 1 / planning_limit_factor (1.25 at 0.80). Existing load is served up to it
operating_limit.source: Derived: the full feeder rating relative to 0.80 x rating (contract reserves ignored) Dominion value used as a proxy until this utility's own feeder data is found.

subband_enabled.unit: per-utility switch: carve a constrained sub-band (load above the planning limit) out of the most loaded bands; on in every scenario (a scenario's network values or NETWORK_OVERRIDES can switch it off)

subband_load_share.unit: share of network load in the constrained sub-band
subband_load_share.source: Dominion Energy Virginia, Grid Utilization Metrics Proposal, SCC Case No. PUR-2026-00164 (filed 15 Oct 2026), Metric (iv): 82 of ~1,900 feeders (4.3%) exceed 100% planning utilisation at their local peak. Feeder share used as a proxy for load share Dominion value used as a proxy until this utility's own feeder data is found.

subband_utilisation.unit: starting planning utilisation of the constrained sub-band
subband_utilisation.source: Midpoint of the planning limit (1.00) and the operating limit (1.25); the filing gives only the count of feeders above 100%, not their loading Dominion value used as a proxy until this utility's own feeder data is found.

upgrade_delay_ordinary_years.unit: Upgrade Delay for Interconnection, ordinary new load (EVs, heat pumps, small business) in constrained areas: years from request to connection (fractional years split between the two whole years)
upgrade_delay_ordinary_years.source: RG&E publishes no connection timeline for constrained areas (NYSEG/RG&E, Powering New York, NYSAC presentation, Jul 2025: 45% of RG&E substation transformers constrained, average load request ~1 MVA; no timeline). Con Edison guide used as the New York proxy. Con Edison, E-Mobility Interconnection Guide: New & Upgraded Electric Service Overview (coned.com, rev. 30 Apr 2026): project timeline from service determination to energization, including any upstream utility modifications and transformer or feeder reinforcement: <300 kW overhead / <500 kW underground 4-6 months; 300-2,000 kW 12-18 months; 500-5,000 kW network and 2,000-10,000 kW 24-36 months; >8,000 kW high-tension 36+ months. Low 0.5 / central 1.5 / high 3.0 yr

upgrade_delay_large_years.unit: Upgrade Delay for Interconnection, large loads (data centres on the distribution system, fleet hubs) in constrained areas: years from request to connection
upgrade_delay_large_years.source: RG&E publishes no connection timeline for constrained areas (NYSEG/RG&E, Powering New York, NYSAC presentation, Jul 2025: 45% of RG&E substation transformers constrained, average load request ~1 MVA; no timeline). Con Edison guide used as the New York proxy. Large loads: Con Edison guide low 2.0 yr (24 months), central 3.0 yr (36+ months, >8 MW); high 6.0 yr from Dominion Energy Virginia, Application for approval of large-load connection queue process standards, SCC Case No. PUR-2026-00011 (filed 2 Feb 2026), para. 5-6: ~25,000 MW of large-load delivery-point requests (>= ~100 MW, data centres) assigned projected connection dates through 31 Dec 2031; a further ~45,000 MW batched and still being studied; ~10 new requests (2,000-3,000 MW) a month

backlog_clearance_pct.unit: share of the outstanding constrained backlog (existing load above the planning limit) the utility clears per year, in service the following year; replaces clearing as soon as lead time and build rate allow
backlog_clearance_pct.source: No utility publishes a clearance rate for constrained feeders. Low 6%/yr: Dominion Energy Virginia, Application for approval of large-load connection queue process standards, SCC Case No. PUR-2026-00011 (filed 2 Feb 2026), para. 5-6: ~25,000 MW of large-load delivery-point requests (>= ~100 MW, data centres) assigned projected connection dates through 31 Dec 2031; a further ~45,000 MW batched and still being studied; ~10 new requests (2,000-3,000 MW) a month - about 25 of 70 GW given dates over the ~6 years to 2031, ~6% of the backlog a year (large loads, transmission). Central 20%/yr (backlog cleared in about 5 years) is an assumption between that and high 33%/yr (cleared within the 3-year central reinforcement lead time, close to the earlier model assumption)

constrained_build_priority.unit: constrained areas get build-rate priority: their upgrades are not capped by max_build_pct (false = backlog clearance and new-load upgrades together capped at max_build_pct of the band capacity per year)
constrained_build_priority.source: Model setting (overloaded feeders are relieved first for reliability)

planning_headroom.unit: firm network capacity above network peak, share
planning_headroom.source: No published system-wide figure. Con Edison publishes feeder hosting/load-capacity maps (coned.com/en/business-partners/hosting-capacity); Pepco must file feeder-level constraint data under COMAR 20.50.15. Neither is aggregated to a system headroom %.

reinforcement_lead_years.unit: years from order to in service
reinforcement_lead_years.source: Assumption: distribution feeder and substation reinforcement typically takes 2-5 years

max_build_pct.unit: maximum reinforcement ordered per year, share of capacity

seed_pipeline.unit: projects under way at 2026: 'derived' = the next lead-time years of network growth with planning headroom, allocated to bands by growth share (keeps the 2026 growth / asset-condition capex split independent of the bands); 'none'; or [{year, mw}]
seed_pipeline.source: Model calibration; no utility publishes its in-flight distribution capacity pipeline in MW

constrained_loading.unit: loading above which a band counts as constrained
constrained_loading.source: Dominion Energy Virginia, Grid Utilization Metrics Proposal, SCC Case No. PUR-2026-00164 (filed 15 Oct 2026), Section 4.3: substation-transformer zones at their own local peak average 79.8% planning utilisation (78.3% general; capacity net of a 0.70 x largest-transformer N-1 reserve); 82 of ~1,900 feeders (4.3%) exceed 100% planning utilisation (load / (0.80 x rating - contract reserves)), the filing's definition of a constrained feeder (constrained = above 100% planning utilisation)

flex_targeting_enabled.unit: site flexible headroom first in bands above their planning limit; false = pro rata (flex_share)
flex_targeting_enabled.source: Model setting (policy lever: locational targeting of flexibility)

flex_targeting_share.unit: maximum share of flexible headroom sited in bands above their planning limit when targeting is on (never more than the load above the limit); 1.0 = those bands first

bau_plan.label: Published-plan BAU
bau_plan._note: BAU distribution capex from the utility's published capital plan, split by category, with addressable shares; transmission from its own plan where it is a separate bill line. engine.layers.plan_paths().

basis.source: Setting. 'published_plan': BAU distribution capex follows the utility's published capital plan, and the network model estimates how much of the plan's growth-driven spending flexibility could defer. 'model': BAU capex generated by the network model (reinforcement for load growth + asset-condition capex), the basis before this change.

plan_years.source: Years covered by the Case 25-E-0379 capital forecast (see plan_dist_capex_m).

plan_dist_capex_m.unit: $M nominal per year (distribution, incl. transmission recovered in delivery)
plan_dist_capex_m.source: RG&E electric capital as proposed in Case 25-E-0379 (final order pending): $308.4M (2026) and $420.6M (2027) (Staff Initial Post-Evidentiary Hearing Brief, Cases 25-E-0375 et al., citing the Companies' proposal; Staff recommends $226.3M and $246.1M); 2026-2031 total RG&E Electric $5.06B (Investment Planning and Common Capital Expenditures Panel rebuttal testimony, 5 Dec 2025; $5.03B as filed), so 2028-2031 = ($5,060M - $729.0M) / 4 = $1,082.75M a year (equal split: the annual profile is in Exhibit IPCC-6R, not read). Each year less the hydro generation share (14,735 / 336,163 = 4.4%, 2026 Five-Year Plan) plus RG&E common capital ($471.6M 2026-2031, electric allocation 71.39%, = $56.1M a year): $351.0M, $458.3M, then $1091.4M a year. Replaces the single 2026 Five-Year Plan year ($385.2M) and the Con Edison CAGR proxy.

plan_cagr_override.source: Growth rate carried beyond 2031 for the continue and taper paths: 0%, because the published total gives 2028-2031 as a flat average (the endpoint CAGR, 25.5% a year 2026-2031, reflects the ramp to the plan's later years, not a trend to extend). Replaces the Con Edison 7.2% proxy.

beyond_path.source: Setting. Distribution capex beyond the plan horizon: 'continue' = plan CAGR; 'taper' = growth tapers linearly from the plan CAGR to load growth (BAU network peak growth, nominal) by taper_year; 'policy' = nominal network peak growth with electrification at its high level (state electrification and clean energy plans).

taper_year.source: Setting: year by which capex growth has tapered to load growth (taper path).

category_shares.unit: shares of distribution capex: growth, replacement, grid modernisation / resilience, other
category_shares.source: NYSEG and RG&E, Capital Investment Plan Quarterly Variance Report Q1 2026 (NYPSC, May 2026), Figure 3, RG&E Electric and Generation Five-Year Plan 2026 ($000, before common costs), hydro generation 14,735 excluded: growth = Customer Focus 83,074; replacement = Asset Condition 62,710 + Reliability 107,781 = 170,491; grid modernisation / resilience = Modernization 1,145 + Resiliency 19,882 + Innovation 2,661 + AMI 3,002 = 26,690; other = Compliance 41,172; total 321,427. Mapping is the model's.

addressable_growth.source: Setting. Cap on the share of the plan's growth-driven capex that flexibility, efficiency and better planning could defer; the share actually deferred each year is the network model's cumulative reinforcement avoided vs BAU, up to this cap. Central 0.80 = the earlier model's NWS_AVOIDANCE_OF_ELIGIBLE_MATURE (Brattle, Value of Using DERs for Distribution System Services in Ontario, 2026: NWS cost-effective in 95% of feeder scenarios); low 0.5 / high 1.0 bracket it.

addressable_replacement.source: Setting: share of asset-replacement capex right-sized when assets are replaced (smaller transformers, cables and substation equipment where flexibility and efficiency lower the load the replacement must serve). Range 10% / 20% / 30% as specified for the sensitivity; no utility publishes a right-sizing share.

addressable_gridmod.unit: share of grid modernisation / resilience capex
addressable_gridmod.source: Setting: share of grid modernisation and resilience capex that better planning could avoid or right-size (most of it is reliability-driven and stays). 0% / 5% / 10%.

addressable_other.source: Setting: other capex (public works relocations, environmental, compliance, safety) is not addressable.

addressable_ramp_years.source: Setting: years from the transition year over which right-sizing of replacement, grid modernisation and other capex ramps in (programmes and planning practice take time to reach full effect).

link_growth_to_load.source: Setting. True (central): the growth-driven category of plan capex is scaled, year by year in the plan years, by the model's cumulative system peak growth since 2026 relative to the load growth the plan assumes (plan_load_growth). False: plan capex fixed regardless of load. Replacement, grid modernisation and other categories stay on plan either way.

plan_load_growth.source: NYISO 2026 Load & Capacity Data Report (Gold Book), Table I-3a: Zone B summer coincident peak 1,828 MW (2026) to 2,122 MW (2031) = 3.03% a year, including Table I-14 large loads (Zone B 11 MW to 411 MW by 2030). Proxy: RG&E's own forecast behind its Case 25-E-0379 capital plan was not found; Zone B also includes National Grid's Genesee territory.

electrification_pace.source: Setting (electrification pace). 'utility_forecast' (central): BAU load is calibrated to the load forecast behind the utility's published plan (plan_load_growth over the plan years) by scaling electrification growth (kept >= 0) and, if needed, lowering baseline growth; the growth-capex scale factor is then 1.0 in the last plan year. 'state_policy': the model's electrification assumptions (notebook ELECTRIFICATION_RAMP, state policy pace), which grow load faster than most utility forecasts.

capacity_carve_out.source: NYISO Rest of State (RG&E is in Load Zone B) monthly spot capacity prices, 2026: May $8.00, Jul $4.14, Sep $5.97/kW-month (Modo Energy NYISO monthly reports); mean $6.0367/kW-month x 12 = $0.07244M/MW-yr. v1.0 uses NYISO.json zone G_H_I ($0.070M/MW-yr) for RG&E; that default is unchanged. Peak: RGE.json. Residential share and customers: EIA-861 2024. Scaling 1.0 (NYISO reserve margin not applied).
capacity_carve_out.method: Residential capacity obligation per customer = peak_mw x residential_share x obligation_scaling / residential_customers; $/month = obligation (kW) x price ($/kW-day) x 365/12. Assumes the residential share of the obligation equals its share of sales (residential load is peakier, so this likely understates it). The amount is moved out of the parent line(s); the total bill is unchanged.
